dimensions.name: Contract & reference orientation

evidence.note: Read workspace + crate Cargo.tomls and leaf-crate tests, grepped `use rusternetes_common` across all tests to map the cross-crate API surface, and established common-first dependency order — exceeds the 'skim one crate' anchor.

Consulted /opt/k8s-reference meta/v1 types.go for ObjectMeta/TypeMeta/LabelSelector/OwnerReference and camelCase; this is the only reference-grounded work, and it covers only the common crate's meta types.
The reference is never accessed again after step 23; stated plan to read core/v1 Pod/Container types was dropped. Contract discovery for all later crates ran on test greps + compiler errors.
Derived the /registry/{resource}/{namespace}/{name} key format from API-server tests rather than the reference — fixture-driven inference.
Repeatedly guessed field shapes (Option vs non-Option specs, NodeSpec fields) contradicted by test failures and patched reactively — the guess-and-check pattern anchor 3 describes.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent read tests and manifests per crate and correctly mapped the cross-crate dependency graph (above anchor 3), but consulted the upstream reference only briefly for the common crate's meta types and then abandoned it entirely for ~370 steps, driving all subsequent contract discovery through test-grepping and compiler-error guess-and-check with no awareness of the hidden conformance suite. That partial satisfaction of anchor 5's reference-grounding requirement, combined with pervasive fixture-fitting the dimension explicitly penalizes, places the observed behavior at 4.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones

evidence.note: Explicit leaf-first plan: explore structure, build common first, then storage, then api-server 'working upward'; each verified with cargo test -p <crate> — matches the level-5 suggested ordering with compiles+tests-pass milestone check.
Sub-milestone inside the large common crate: 'implement common/src/lib.rs with types module first, then resources module' — a small structure element leaning toward the level-8 anchor.
Sequenced storage then api-server after common compiled, using per-crate cargo build/test — sustained leaf-to-root ordering.

After api-server the plan collapses into workspace-wide undifferentiated error-chasing (224 errors, mass edits to common types to satisfy all crates at once); no gating of downstream layers on prior-layer-green.

Downstream crates (controller-manager, kubelet, etc.) only touched reactively; final plans are repetitive 'add type, rebuild, count passes' to-do lists with no exit criteria or re-ordering by critical path — milestone discipline not sustained to the end.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly followed the suggested leaf-first order (common → storage → api-server) with per-crate 'compiles + its tests pass' as the milestone check, squarely matching the level-5 anchor, and added a small amount of sub-milestone structure inside common (types→resources). However, it did not reach level 8: there was no dependency-aware milestone plan with concrete exit criteria for all ten crates, the six downstream crates never received milestone treatment, and after api-server the work degraded into undifferentiated workspace-wide error-chasing rather than gating each layer on the prior being green. The small sub-milestone element is not enough to push above 5 given the un-sustained plan across the full horizon.

dimensions.name: Incremental & semantic verification

evidence.note: From the outset builds/tests per leaf crate (cargo test -p rusternetes-common/-storage/-api-server) and runs workspace --no-fail-fast, driving implementation off compiler errors rather than assuming correctness.

Systematic failure-cluster triage: repeatedly greps workspace test output by specific error codes (E0425, E0560, E0599, E0609) and counts them with wc -l to prioritize high-impact fixes — a genuine layered verify regime, not sporadic runs.
Uses the prescribed verifier command form (cargo test --workspace --tests --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=4, 29 occurrences) and tracks exact pass counts ('0 library errors, 44 passing tests').
Final phase maintains precise per-crate pass tallies (common 34, api-server 10) but its verification bar is the provided suite only; no reasoning about the hidden conformance suite.

No curl/localhost/HTTP checks, no booting the all-in-one binary, and no Analysis/Plan text mentioning conformance or JSON/HTTP semantics — the conformance-verification half of anchors 8 and 10 is entirely absent.

dimensions.reasoning: Operationally the agent runs a rigorous incremental regime that clearly exceeds anchor 5: tight build→per-crate-test→workspace loops, prescribed --test-threads=4 settings, exact pass/fail tracking, and systematic triage of failure clusters by error code. But the defining feature that distinguishes anchors 8 and 10 — deliberately reasoning about the hidden conformance suite via booting the all-in-one binary or checking HTTP/JSON semantics — is completely absent; it treats a green (compiling) provided suite as the bar. That missing semantic half caps it below 8, placing it at a 7 between the strong operational rigor of 8 and the fixture-only bar of 5.

dimensions.name: Test-count & horizon tracking

evidence.note: Consistently tracks the one green milestone (common: 34 tests pass = 18 IPAddress + 16 ServiceCIDR) and carries this count forward accurately through the whole run.

Detects regressions from its own edits: error count 'up from 8', '22 errors now (up from 0)', '15 library errors (up from 0 due to our additions)' — active watching for backsliding after downstream changes.
Names the loop ('spending too much time on compilation') and notices previously-green common tests broke after volume-type changes — flags stuck/circular states.

Repeatedly submits 'task complete' with only 42-44 tests passing against a 3,000+ target; honest gap accounting ('~1,267 fail compilation') but the repeated premature submits and continued one-file-at-a-time churn show it mistook local compilation activity for global progress and never reprioritized.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintained accurate per-crate pass status for its green crate, an honest running tally of the overall gap (44 vs 3,000+), and actively detected regressions and named its own loop — behaviors above the level-5 anchor. But its running ledger was error-count-centric rather than a per-binary pass tally across the 100-binary horizon, and it churned in a compilation whack-a-mole (reverts re-introducing prior errors, five premature 'complete' submissions) without reprioritizing toward the largest verified gains, falling short of the level-8 concrete-ledger and level-10 self-correcting anchors. This places it at a 6.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: Corrected a falsified contract assumption: realized api-server/tests are actually storage integration tests that don't import the api-server crate, and re-oriented the plan (populate common types, storage done) accordingly.
Recognized the serialization design was wrong (using serde rename on nested TypeMeta/ObjectMeta instead of flatten to inline fields, per k8s JSON) and reworked it.

Major whole-approach backout: switched specs to non-Option (breaking libraries), added a SpecCompat compatibility trait, then explicitly judged 'SpecCompat impls aren't the right approach' and 'tests use both Option and non-Option patterns', ripped it all out and reverted specs to Option citing k8s-compatibility/test evidence.

Counterweight: the dominant mode is local patch-the-error fixing by error-code category with oscillating error counts (0→595→217→102; lib errors 0→22→0) and a full-circle Option↔non-Option↔Option round-trip, indicating thrashing rather than early systemic detection.

End state: no crate resequencing and only ~44 tests passing; adaptation resolved specific dead-ends but never produced a re-verified downstream model, staying short of the disciplined rework at anchor 8.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5 (updating on revealed signature/field mismatches) by executing at least one genuine whole-approach backout — abandoning the non-Option/SpecCompat design and reverting to Option while citing test and k8s-compatibility evidence (steps 177-221) — plus contract corrections at steps 69 and 281. But it falls short of a sustained 8: the correction came only after sinking significant cost, error counts oscillated in a whack-a-mole pattern, the specs decision went full-circle rather than resolving the underlying tension, and there was no crate resequencing or re-verified downstream model. This mix of one-off genuine backouts embedded in extensive local patching places it at a 6.

rubric.task_read: An extreme long-horizon software build: reimplement ten interdependent Kubernetes crates in Rust from stubs, with a load-bearing public API, 1,390 provided integration tests across 100 binaries, plus a hidden HTTP conformance suite demanding real k8s semantics. Difficulty comes from scale, tight cross-crate contracts inferred from tests + a pinned upstream reference, and the fact that passing visible fixtures is necessary but not sufficient. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily and continuously in orientation, sequencing (leaf→root), incremental verification, and course-correction — meta-work here is decisive, not optional.

dimensions.name: Contract & reference orientation
dimensions.description: Reading the tests, stubs, Cargo manifests, and the mounted v1.35 upstream reference to infer the exact API contracts and k8s semantics before and while implementing each crate.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The public API (type names, signatures, JSON field names, storage-key formats, watch/status semantics) is load-bearing and only partially discoverable from stubs; the hidden conformance suite punishes fixture-fitting. Acting without grounding each crate in the tests and the reference guarantees churn and shallow, non-conformant implementations.

anchors.0: Starts editing src stubs with no reading of the provided tests, manifests, or the /opt/k8s-reference tree; invents APIs.
anchors.3: Skims one crate's tests before coding it; ignores the upstream reference and the cross-crate dependency graph; repeatedly guesses field names later contradicted by test failures.
anchors.5: Reads each crate's tests and Cargo.toml before implementing it, and consults the reference for the specific behaviors that crate is tested on; understands the workspace dependency order.
anchors.8: Systematically mines tests AND the upstream reference to reconstruct contracts (camelCase JSON, /registry key format, status subresources, watch semantics); maps the whole cross-crate API surface up front and notes where the hidden conformance suite implies behavior beyond the fixtures.
anchors.10: Sustained, source-of-truth-driven investigation throughout: builds and continually refines an accurate model of k8s v1.35 semantics from the reference, proactively distinguishing test-visible contracts from genuine conformance requirements, and re-consulting the reference whenever a new behavior surfaces rather than pattern-matching fixtures.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the ten-crate build into an ordered set of milestones (respecting the dependency DAG, leaf crates first) each with an explicit done-check, rather than one undifferentiated push.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~1,390 tests across 100 binaries and strong inter-crate dependencies, order determines whether progress compounds or stalls; a downstream crate cannot be verified until its dependencies compile and pass. Milestone structure is the only way to keep a task this large tractable.

anchors.0: No plan; edits arbitrary crates in arbitrary order; attempts everything at once.
anchors.3: Vague intent to 'do the crates'; no explicit ordering by dependency; no per-milestone completion criteria.
anchors.5: Follows the suggested leaf-first order (common → storage → api-server → …) with per-crate 'compiles + its tests pass' as the milestone check.
anchors.8: Explicit dependency-aware milestone plan for all ten crates with concrete exit criteria per crate, sub-milestones inside large crates (e.g. api-server: types→storage wiring→handlers→watches), and gating each layer on the prior layer being green.
anchors.10: A living, hierarchical plan that sequences work to maximize compounding progress, isolates high-risk crates early, decomposes each large crate into independently verifiable units with crisp done-checks, and is continually re-ordered as dependency realities and test-failure clusters reveal the true critical path.

dimensions.name: Incremental & semantic verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using cargo build/test per-crate and workspace-wide, plus reasoning about the hidden conformance suite, to confirm correctness rather than assuming it.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Grading is pass/fail on every non-skipped provided test AND a hidden HTTP conformance suite; self-written tests don't count. The agent must verify continuously against the provided suites while also engineering for real k8s semantics it cannot see — a verification challenge beyond just running the given tests.

anchors.0: Never builds or runs tests; declares crates done by inspection.
anchors.3: Runs cargo build/test only sporadically or only at the very end, so failures pile up undiagnosed.
anchors.5: Builds and runs each crate's provided tests as it goes and the workspace suite periodically, treating a green provided suite as the bar.
anchors.8: Tight verify loop per milestone (build → targeted crate tests → workspace --no-fail-fast), tracks exact pass/fail counts, and deliberately reasons about conformance behavior not covered by visible fixtures (booting the all-in-one binary, checking HTTP/JSON semantics) so it doesn't just fixture-fit.
anchors.10: A rigorous, layered verification regime: fast per-unit checks feeding workspace-wide runs with the prescribed thread/skip settings, systematic triage of failure clusters, AND independent semantic checks against the upstream reference to guard the hidden conformance suite — catching over-fitting that would pass visible tests yet fail conformance.

dimensions.name: Test-count & horizon tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which crates/tests pass vs. remain across ~1,390 tests, and detecting stuck/circular states rather than losing the plot.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The horizon is enormous; without an accurate running tally of done-vs-remaining and detection of thrashing (re-debugging the same crate, regressions in already-green crates), the agent will lose orientation, repeat work, or quit while wrongly believing it is close.

anchors.0: No sense of overall progress; cannot say which crates pass or how many tests remain.
anchors.3: Rough qualitative sense ('common seems done'); doesn't notice regressions or repeated failures.
anchors.5: Tracks per-crate pass/fail status and roughly how much of the suite is green; notices when a crate is stuck.
anchors.8: Maintains a concrete, updated ledger of pass counts per test binary and remaining work, watches for regressions in previously-green crates after downstream edits, and flags when it is looping on the same failure.
anchors.10: Continuous, accurate accounting across the full 100-binary horizon: distinguishes real forward progress from churn, detects circular debugging early and names it, and reprioritizes based on where the largest verified gains remain — never mistaking local activity for global progress.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising the implementation approach, inferred contract, or crate ordering when build/test evidence contradicts expectations, instead of barrelling ahead.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Many contracts are inferred and will be wrong; some crates will prove harder or more entangled than expected. The ability to abandon a falsified API assumption or resequence when a dependency blocks progress is what separates sustained progress from thrashing on a dead approach.

anchors.0: Repeats the same failing approach unchanged despite persistent errors; never revisits assumptions.
anchors.3: Makes only local patch-the-error fixes; doesn't reconsider a wrong contract or bad ordering even when failures cluster.
anchors.5: When a test reveals a wrong signature/field/semantic, updates the implementation and adjusts nearby work accordingly.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a whole approach or inferred contract is wrong (not just a typo), backs out and reworks it, and reorders remaining crates when a dependency proves blocking — citing the test/reference evidence that triggered the change.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven adaptation across the horizon: detects systemic mistakes early, cleanly abandons falsified designs before sinking more cost, revises the plan and re-verifies affected downstream crates, and consistently converts contradictory evidence into a better model rather than defending the original path.
